title: Mouse Without Borders fails to pair: "Could not load or update pairing" (Negotiation → Connecting → Error)

inferences: The supplied untrusted-signature entry supports the signer-rejection class for that participant; not every same-text pairing failure is proven to share the identical cause.
initial_investigation: Read complete body, all replies and cross-references, including the latest manual workaround report.

Rechecked the open/unmerged status and intended signer-policy change in51789. Prior exact-release verification established that SettingsSync endpoint verification precedes pairing requests; no community script was executed.
issue_context.summary: Pairing failures have an existing signer-verification investigation and an open candidate PR; no shipped repair is established.
known_information: The full report and discussion describe pairing failure on matching versions despite firewall, network, key and elevation checks; a participant supplies the engine-side untrusted-signature rejection.

The latest November 2 reply reports success after manually mixing executable versions. Other participants report both success and failure with that unofficial workaround; it is not a supported product repair.
The contributor explicitly links PR51789, and its current description targets this issue by replacing identical-leaf-certificate matching with independent trusted Microsoft signature checks.
Live PR51789 is open and unmerged. Issue50795 tracks the same demonstrated rejection class.
issue_context.analysis: The thread now has an explicit proposed fix and owner. Keep its useful diagnosis and connect reports to the existing work instead of creating a competing implementation or asking everyone to repeat network checks. Do not equate an open PR, contributor test claim, or mixed-version workaround with a released fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open candidate fix51789 explicitly targets51567; this is ownership/coverage, not a merged or shipped repair.

comment.body: Thanks for the additional report. The untrusted-signature failure discussed here is tracked in #50795, and #51789 is the open candidate fix explicitly targeting this issue. That PR is not merged or shipped yet. The reports about combining executables from two releases are useful diagnostic evidence, but they do not establish a supported repair or long-term compatibility; we should not ask other users to replace binaries or bypass peer verification. There is no need to repeat the firewall and pairing checks already documented in this thread. Validation of the candidate fix should use a consistent signed build on both computers.
